independent.summary: Refusal records interpolate unbounded client-controlled values (`requestId` from `body.id`, `caller.ua`, `caller.client`) with no truncation, and on /mcp and /bridge/mcp they are now emitted at the default `light` tier *before* the bearer gate passes — so an unauthenticated caller can write ~100KB (express' default JSON body limit) of chosen content per request into the deployed log, where the old 401 path printed one fixed short line; `shortSession` truncates the session id but nothing truncates these.

The `bridge_session_header_ignored` / `stateless_server_mismatch` record — the exact diagnosis the item asks for ("why the session id was rejected — … stateless-server mismatch") — is logged at the `normal` tier, and the same holds for `mcp_delete_unknown_session` (mcp.js:765), while both routers default to `light` (BRIDGE_LOG_LEVEL/MCP_LOG_LEVEL unset), so in a deployed process a repeat of the incident (a chat still presenting stale session ids) leaves no record at all unless someone has raised the level in advance; docs/architecture.md states refusal records go out at `light` and lists this record in that same paragraph, so the doc overstates what the deployment actually logs.

triageGrades.reason: The diff rewrites both endpoints' bearer-gate refusals (401/503 bodies, WWW-Authenticate relocation) and the session scope-mismatch 403, so the auth path is genuinely touched.

The change adds credential-handling code in logging — `callerView()` reads the Authorization header and classifies it, the rejected-header line is deliberately kept at `verbose`, and the diff ships assertions that "a record must never carry the token" — which is secret-handling, not an untouched area.
Nothing in the diff touches billing, usage metering, or paid model calls.

mcp.js:695 is the in-memory session map teardown, whose semantics are unchanged (only a `rememberClosed`/log added) and which destroys no persisted or user data, so no destructive operation is touched.
No outbound HTTP or third-party API call is added or changed; the MCP SDK transport is in-process.
No version bump, deploy config, migration, or release artifact is touched — only server source, tests, and docs.
